runs.text: Product differentiation provides variety that consumers value, but firms may produce below the quantity that minimizes average total cost. Assess the benefit of a better product match alongside higher unit costs and markups. Productive efficiency alone does not measure the full welfare effect of variety.

transcript.sourceText: WORKED EXAMPLE: WEIGHING THE VALUE OF VARIETY
transcript.text: WORKED EXAMPLE: WEIGHING THE VALUE OF VARIETY

runs.text: Two bakeries offer different breads. A neighborhood values having both varieties, but dividing sales between the bakeries can leave each producing below its lowest-cost scale. More variety can therefore benefit buyers while raising cost per loaf. A welfare judgment weighs those benefits against the extra resource cost; a markup alone does not measure the value of variety.

Outcome: Evaluate Product Variety, Efficiency & Model Limits.
Difficulty: Advanced
THE CORE IDEA

Product differentiation provides variety that consumers value, but firms may produce below the quantity that minimizes average total cost. Assess the benefit of a better product match alongside higher unit costs and markups. Productive efficiency alone does not measure the full welfare effect of variety.
HOW TO RECOGNIZE IT
More varieties can better match different preferences.
Smaller production runs can raise average cost.
Compare the value of variety with costs and markups before judging welfare.
WATCH OUT
Differentiation can create consumer value through variety even when the standard model shows some productive inefficiency.
WORKED EXAMPLE: WEIGHING THE VALUE OF VARIETY

Two bakeries offer different breads. A neighborhood values having both varieties, but dividing sales between the bakeries can leave each producing below its lowest-cost scale. More variety can therefore benefit buyers while raising cost per loaf. A welfare judgment weighs those benefits against the extra resource cost; a markup alone does not measure the value of variety.
